lines.text: Do you know how popcorn pops? Every kernel is a tiny pressure cooker.
Inside the hard shell is soft starch, and a little bit of water, about fourteen percent.
Heat it, and the water turns to steam. The shell is so tough that the steam can't get out.
At around one hundred eighty degrees, the pressure inside is about nine times the air around us. The shell bursts.
The hot starch puffs out like foam and sets in a split second, turning the kernel inside out.
Kernels that have dried out don't have enough steam, so they never pop.
